rated_messages.input_message: Take a deep breath and let it out slowly. Notice that you are completely OK for this one breath. Do it again.
Life can get you really stressed out, but turning to cigs isn't the answer. Call or text family and friends instead. Ask them to help you stay on track.
Just because other people are smoking, doesn't mean you have to. Practice allowing this urge to be present for 5 minutes. When it passes, give yourself credit.
Don't test yourself needlessly. If this social situation gets uncomfortable then leave briefly if you can. It really helps and it's fine to do it more than once!
One way to combat any urges is to keep your mouth busy - some people find that chewing sugar free gum, mints, or even a pen can be a good alternative.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.

The best way to deal with any urges from being around smokers is to get out of the situation briefly until it goes. Make an excuse, go to the toilet, go get some water, pretend you need to get some phone reception!
Just because letting an urge pass isn't easy, doesn't mean that you can't do it. Try it, you might surprise yourself.
If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, keep a pen and paper nearby to occupy your hands with doodling rather than smoking.
